properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 3:07PM PST until November 18 at 4:30PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Coastal San Francisco Peninsula

* WHEN...Until 430 PM PST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 307 PM PST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. This  will
cause urban and small stream flooding. Between 0.5 and 2.5 inches
of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.2 to 0.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
San Francisco, Daly City, Pacifica, Half Moon Bay, El Granada,
Moss Beach, Montara and Broadmoor.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM; Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 18 at 6:02PM EST until November 18 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

* Until 700 PM EST.

* At 602 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 26 nm southeast of Carysfort Reef Light,
moving northwest at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.areaDesc: North Central and Southeast Siskiyou County
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 18 at 2:58PM PST until November 19 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Winter Storm Warning, additional snow accumulations
between 2 and 4 inches. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph. For the
Winter Weather Advisory, additional snow accumulations up to one
inch.

* WHERE...The Winter Storm Warning includes the Shasta highlands and
Medicine Lake. The Winter Weather Advisory includes portions of
highway 97 between Grass Lake and Macdoel, and the area around Bray
and Tennant.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. The hazardous
conditions will impact this evenings commute. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 2:30PM PST until November 18 at 5:30PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Timber burn area...

* Until 530 PM PST.

* At 230 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the Timber Burn Area. Between 1 and 2
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to
0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the Drainages within
Lafler, Castro and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between
Grimes and Castro Canyons. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Timber Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Timber Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from
Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of
Big Sur.
properties.instruction:
Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, and roads is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain. Impacted
areas include locations along Highway 1 near mile marker 50 south of
Andrew Molera State Park to mile maker 38. Other areas impacted
include Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park Campground and Partington Ridge,
structures along the Big Sur River, Mule Creek Canyon, and adjacent
drainages and watershed outlets.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 18 at 4:30PM EST by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Thursday, for the Mon
Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

For more information on ground-level ozone and
fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and
https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

in case you become stranded.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Pooling of sea

that is uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach
erosion is also possible. No significant damage is expected.

early morning high tide. Additional hazardous surf and coastal
flooding isues are expected next week.
properties.instruction:

near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 11:28AM PST until November 20 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-
18 feet, with local sets of 18 to 22 feet. Peak surf is
expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous rip
currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate
coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...From 9 PM this evening to 3 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially
to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through
the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous
surf and coastal flooding isues are expected next week.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 18 at 1:16PM CST until November 19 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Thursday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide
at 1049 PM tonight, 1104 AM Thursday, and 1041 Thursday night.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Avalanche Watch issued November 18 at 9:10AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
AVAREV

The following message is transmitted at the request of the U.S.
Forest Service Sierra Avalanche Center.

BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WATCH

IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED

08:55 PST Wed Nov 18 2026

The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY
AVALANCHE WATCH for the following areas:
NWS Reno NV - NVZ002 (Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA))

* WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger is anticipated in the backcountry
from around sunset on Wednesday into early Friday morning.

* WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy
49) on the north and Ebbetts Pass(Hwy 4) on the south,
including the greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to
backcountry areas, not to ski areas and highways where avalanche
mitigation programs exist.

* WHEN...In effect from Wed 08:55 PST to Thu 05:00 PST.

* IMPACTS...Significant snowfall may lead to widespread avalanche
activity in the mountains. Large avalanches capable of burying
or injuring people could occur in backcountry areas.

* PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous
avalanche conditions could occur in the backcountry. Traveling
in, near, or below backcountry avalanche terrain during HIGH
avalanche danger is not recommended.

Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or
www.avalanche.org for more detailed information.

Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside
the coverage area of this or any avalanche center.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.instruction:

promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 18 at 9:01AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Total snow accumulations between 1 to 3 feet
expected above this elevation; accumulations around 4 feet above
8,000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday
morning commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13
to 17 ft. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 18
to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored breakpoints along the
coast from this afternoon through Friday morning.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.
properties.instruction:

conditions.

infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 18 at 8:08AM PST until November 18 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12
to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored
breakpoints along the coast from this afternoon through Friday
morning.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday.
These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will
enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide
varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast
and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 18 at 9:00AM EST by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Wednesday, for the
Mon Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

For more information on ground-level ozone and
fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and
https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued November 18 at 2:32AM MST until November 18 at 5:00PM MST by NWS Cheyenne WY
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 9 AM THIS MORNING TO 5 PM MST THIS
AFTERNOON DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR PORTIONS OF NE
AND WY...

The National Weather Service in Cheyenne WY has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from 9 AM this morning to 5 PM MST this afternoon.

* AFFECTED AREA...In southeast Wyoming, fire weather zones 430
through 433. In western Nebraska, fire weather zones 436 and 437.

* TIMING...From 9 AM this morning to 5 PM MST this afternoon.

* WINDS...West winds 25 to 40 mph with gusts up to 65 mph in Wyoming
and up to 55 mph in Nebraska.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 14 and 20 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 1:25AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF ADVISORY NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 7 PM EST FRIDAY... ...HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH FRIDAY EVENING

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 18 at 12:30AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Duval, Coastal Flagler, Eastern Clay, Eastern
Putnam, Inland Flagler, Northeast Coastal St. Johns, Northern
Inland St. Johns, South Central Duval, Southeast Coastal St. Johns,
Southern Inland St. Johns, Trout River, Western Clay, Western
Duval, Western Putnam and Western St. Johns.

* WHEN...Through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of heavy rainfall are expected to repeatedly occur
in the watch area through the end of the week. Repeated rounds of
heavy rainfall will result in the potential for urban and small
stream flooding for the coastal areas of northeast Florida. Total
rainfall forecast through Friday night is around 3 to 8 inches
with locally higher amounts up to 12 inches or more.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:

WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR KNOX COUNTY...

The National Weather Service in Omaha/Valley NE has issued a Red Flag
Warning.

* WHAT...Southwest winds 22 to 28 mph with peak gusts up to 40 mph,
Relative Humidity as low as 20 percent.

* WHERE...Knox county.

* WHEN...From noon to 6 PM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:

promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Kenai Mtns
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 17 at 1:32PM AKST until November 19 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by
excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following area, Southern Kenai Mtns. This
includes the city of Seward.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday
morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With
upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 4 inches
of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with
elevation. Rainfall rates of up to a quarter of an inch per hour
are possible between 3PM Wednesday through 3PM Thursday.
Southerly to southeasterly winds will shift to more easterly
early Thursday morning, limiting precipitation amounts in lee of
the mountains for areas along the Seward Highway from roughly
Moose Pass and southward to Seward. Rainfall is on track to
decrease late Thursday afternoon. Prolonged heavy rain may lead
to areas of flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in
low-lying and poor drainage areas, and ponding of water on
roadways.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 16 at 3:18PM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Most of east central Florida, including Volusia, Seminole,
Orange, Osceola, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, Saint Lucie,
and Martin counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Repeated rounds of showers and isolated storms are forecast
through Friday. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches are forecast
with localized higher amounts of 8 to 12 inches. The greatest
potential for these higher amounts will be over the coastal
counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM TUESDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH FRIDAY EVENING
